Common Ground — Reflection

I made Common Ground for people who have something to share but do not always want to post it on social media. That could be a quiet student, an older neighbor with a story, or someone who has just moved to a new place. The idea is that a small memory or useful piece of knowledge deserves a place, even if it will never get much attention.

I wanted to imagine an internet where people could return to things instead of constantly moving on. A memory can change when you talk about it with someone else. You might remember another detail, learn something new, or see the experience differently. In this project, those additions become chapters, and the plant grows as the writing develops.

The feedback helped me realize that the first version looked more like a collection of cards than a garden. It also took too much explanation to understand. I added an actual garden view with a path, a greenhouse, a bench, and plants you can click. The small signs tell you whose story you are opening. There is still a list view for people who prefer to read that way.

I kept the evening colors because I wanted the space to feel calm. Pink, purple, and green flowers stand out against the ground, and their shape changes from a small shoot to a bud and then a flower. The buttons use direct language. A short example shows what happens when you add chapters, and the planting form offers prompts if you are unsure what to write. CSS Flexbox keeps the plants and other sections arranged on both phones and larger screens.

The shared community is still an imagined future. The example stories are fictional, and visitors’ writing stays in their own browser. I think making that distinction clear matters. A real version would need people to decide together how stories are shared, who can respond, and how someone can leave or remove their work.
